title: Future-complete equivalence preserves exact target distance
statement: If S ≡fc S ′ under a strong bisimulation preserving target membership, then dist(S, W) = dist(S ′, W) for unit-cost edges, including infinite values.
proof: Every length-n path from S is matched step for step from S ′, with equivalent endpoint and the same target-membership label. Thus an n-step target path exists from one state exactly when one exists from the other. Their sets of attainable target-path lengths, and therefore their minima, agree.
intended_use: Strengthens a reachability-only reading of safe merging to exact unit-cost distance.

title: Polynomial equivalence preserves polynomially bounded proof families
statement: If two proof systems are polynomially equivalent and a tautology family has polynomial-size proofs in one, then it has polynomial-size proofs in the other.
proof: Use the p-simulation from the first system to the second to translate each proof with polynomial blowup. The polynomial bound composed with a polynomial translator remains polynomial.
intended_use: Turns proof-size upper bounds into degree-level invariants under polynomial equivalence.

title: Safe quotienting preserves bounded target reachability
statement: For any n, equivalent states agree on whether a target is reachable within n steps. The quotient graph has the same target distance as any representative when its transitions are the induced bisimulation-class transitions.
proof: The first assertion follows from equality of distances. For the second, a concrete path projects to a quotient path. A quotient path lifts from any representative: at each edge use bisimulation to match the transition that witnesses that quotient edge. Induction lifts the entire finite path, preserving length and target labels.
intended_use: Prevents a quotient implementation from creating spurious shortcuts by switching representatives without a lifting argument.

title: Injective complete-state recoding preserves the transition system
statement: a Let G be a labeled operational graph. Encode each complete state by e(s), declare e(s) − → e(t) exactly a when s − → t, and transport all observation and ownership labels. Then the graph on e[S] is isomorphic to G and preserves labeled paths, unit target distances, and forced horizons.
hypotheses: an injective encoding e and transported transitions
proof: Injectivity gives an inverse on the image, and the transported edge rule gives a two-way edge correspondence. Paths correspond edge by edge. Target labels and ownership are unchanged, so the same action choices and compatible plays transport controller strategies in both directions with the same lengths.
intended_use: Shows precisely why exact addressing is safe as identity recoding.

title: Adaptive switching among sound navigation policies preserves safety
statement: Allow the controller to switch policies after any finite observed history. If every selected action is still checked against the same legal transition relation and every admitted certificate uses the same sound verifier, every accepted theorem remains a consequence of the current certified premises.
proof: Induct on the accepted chronology. The choice of selector does not alter the legality or verification requirements of the next accepted step. The source safety argument therefore applies at every step, regardless of the switching history.
intended_use: Permits IAE-style adaptive control while isolating the proof-safety obligation.

title: Owner- and target-preserving bisimulation preserves forced horizons
statement: Ownership preservation is an additional explicit hypothesis. Let R be a strong bisimulation between two turn-based graphs that preserves controller/environment ownership and target membership. Matching is required in both directions for every legal successor. Then related states belong to the same finite forced-settlement stages An, and have equal forced horizons (including ∞).
proof: Induct on n. Target preservation gives the claim for A0. At a controller state, a successor in An exists on one side exactly when a matching successor exists on the other, by bisimulation and induction. At an environment state, nonemptiness of the successor set is preserved; every successor is in An on one side exactly when every matching successor is on the other, using both matching directions. Membership in An+1 therefore agrees. Equality of the least finite stage, or absence from all finite stages, follows.
intended_use: Answers one sufficient-conditions version of the strategic- preservation question.

title: The union horizon is attained at a finite BANK stage
statement: If HFinf (B∞, T) = h < ∞, some K satisfies HFinf (BK, T) = h, and every k ≥ K has that same value.
proof: Choose a proof attaining the finite minimum h. Its finite premise support lies in some BK, giving horizon at most h there. Since BK ⊆ B∞, its horizon is at least the union minimum h. The same two inequalities hold for later stages.
intended_use: Connects the limiting resource pool to an actual finite stage.

title: Inference-closed sets are exactly consequence fixed points
statement: For every W ⊆ y, W is inference-closed if and only if ConF (W) = W.
proof: If W is inference-closed, Theorem 1.11 makes ConF (W) the least inference-closed set containing W, so it equals W. Conversely, ConF (W) is always inference-closed; if it equals W, then W is inferenceclosed.
intended_use: Turns closure checking into a fixed-point criterion for the consequence operator.

title: Strict comparison is preserved by equivalent representatives
statement: Define M ≺ N by M ⪯clk N and N ̸⪯clk M. Replacing either endpoint by a mutually simulating machine preserves ≺.
proof: Apply LF-01.1 to the forward comparison and to the reversed comparison, including its negation.
intended_use: Allows strict chains and separation results to be stored at degree level.

title: A strict family separation blocks polynomial equivalence
statement: For the Tseitin family of Theorem 10.44, the stated separation prevents resolution and Polynomial Calculus from being polynomially equivalent under the same proof-size measure.
proof: LF-C10.5 gives the easy translation from resolution to Polynomial Calculus. Theorem 10.44 supplies a family for which the reverse polynomial-size simulation would contradict the stated lower/upper separation.
intended_use: Converts a family-specific size gap into a structural non-equivalence conclusion.

title: Rule-preserved properties hold throughout the consequence closure
statement: If all premises in Γ have property P and every inference rule preserves P, then every member of ConF (Γ) has P.
proof: Supplement Theorem 5 is rule induction on finite derivations.
intended_use: Provides a generic invariant engine for proof systems.

title: Canonical enumeration and breadth-first search agree on theoremhood
statement: For inference-closed Y and Γ ⊆ Y, a formula φ ∈ Y eventually appears in the canonical rule enumerator EF,Y if and only if it lies in some breadth-first proof layer.
proof: Theorem 2.17 says the union of enumerator states is ConF (Γ) ∩ Y. Theorem 2.12 says the union of breadth-first layers is the same set.
intended_use: Shows two different operational chronologies can enumerate the same deductive closure.

title: Recoding preserves exact proof layers
statement: For every m, t[LF (Γ, m)] = LF t (t[Γ], m).
proof: Membership in the left side means exact minimum proof length m before recoding. LF-C04.2 preserves that minimum exactly and t is bijective on the recoded syntax.

title: Recoding preserves exact shortest-proof length
statement: Under the same hypotheses, ∥t(φ)∥F t (t[Γ]) = ∥φ∥F (Γ).
proof: A proof of either side transports to a proof of the same length on the other side. Taking minima in both directions gives equality.
intended_use: Blocks a claimed proof-length speedup obtained only by invertible renaming.

title: Resolution lower bounds and extended-Frege upper bounds yield a two-system size separation
statement: For the pigeonhole family covered by the source theorems, resolution requires the stated exponential-size proofs while ex- tended Frege has polynomial-size proofs; hence the family separates the two systems by proof size.
proof: Combine the lower bound of Theorem 10.17 with the upper bound of Theorem 10.18 on the same family.
intended_use: Provides an unconditional source of proof-size speedup without claiming a wall-clock ATP theorem.

title: Intersections of consequence fixed points are fixed points

title: Recoding preserves derivability
statement: Under an invertible syntactic recoding t, Γ ⊢F φ if and only if t[Γ] ⊢F t t(φ).
proof: Theorem 4.8 transports proofs line by line in both directions using the invertibility of the recoding.

title: Clocked mutual simulation is transitive
statement: If M ∼ N and N ∼ P, then M ∼ P.
proof: Compose the forward simulations M ⪯ N ⪯ P and separately the reverse simulations P ⪯ N ⪯ M using Proposition 3.19.

title: Degeneracy does not descend to admissible equivalence classes
statement: There are admissibly self-awareness-equivalent representatives that disagree on the source nondegeneracy property.
proof: Theorem 21.7 constructs handed equivalent representatives; Corollary 21.8 extracts failure of invariance.

title: State invariants compose over any finite run prefix
statement: If Q holds at the initial state and every ATP transition preserves Q, then Q holds after any finite number of stages.
proof: This is ordinary stage induction supplied by Supplement Theorem 11.
intended_use: Supports invariants about whole search states, not only individual formulas.

title: Equivalence-invariant properties obey parity across equivalent representatives
statement: For any property P satisfying the invariance hypothesis of Proposition 18.21, equivalent tagged systems agree on P.
proof: This is the parity statement of Proposition 18.21.
intended_use: Provides a reusable test for which proposed witness properties descend to quotient classes.

title: Conservation under a countable increasing BANK union
statement: Let B0 ⊆ B1 ⊆ · · · with Bk+1 ⊆ ConF (Bk), and put B∞ = S k Bk. Then ConF (B∞) = ConF (B0).
proof: Repeated road-building gives ConF (Bk) = ConF (B0) for every finite k. Any proof from the union uses finitely many union premises by LF-08.1; all lie in a single BK because the BANKs increase. Its conclusion therefore lies in ConF (B0). The reverse inclusion follows from B0 ⊆ B∞.
intended_use: Extends conservation from each finite deposit stage to the entire accumulated premise pool.

title: Turing equivalence is a statement about effective SICs, not all SICs
statement: The corrected SIC–Turing correspondence cannot be extended to all set-theoretic SICs without additional hypotheses.
proof: LF-TM.B4 gives the correspondence on effective presentations; LF-TM.B5 supplies SICs outside the computable class. A univer- sal extension would contradict that separation.
intended_use: States the exact boundary of the computation analogy.

title: Exact join criterion in the finite static subclass
statement: Work within the finite static constant-halting subclass, where h, u ≥ 0 and h + u is a positive power of two. For a nonempty finite collection S(hi, ui), put a = maxi hi and b = maxi ui. Its join in this subclass exists exactly when a + b is a power of two; in that case the join is S(a, b).
proof: If a + b is a power of two, S(a, b) is an allowed machine. The coordinate criterion makes it an upper bound below every other upper bound. Conversely, let P be the least power of two with P ≥ a + b. Both U = S(a, P − a) and V = S(P − b, b) are allowed upper bounds. Any join J = S(h, u) must lie below both and above all original machines. Thus a ≤ h ≤ a and b ≤ u ≤ b, so J = S(a, b). It is allowed only when a + b is a power of two.
intended_use: Turns the source’s six-state obstruction into a classification for finite static joins.

title: Proof-covering branches recover completeness without making every branch complete
statement: Under proof-covering search, every provable target occurs on at least one branch even if many individual branches miss it forever.
proof: This is the content of the Branch-Covering Theorem: coverage is a property of the branch family, not of every member.
intended_use: Clarifies why heuristic nondeterminism can be complete as an ensemble.

title: A slowly changing rank gives a lower bound on birth stage
statement: Under the theorem’s rank-increment hypothesis, a target whose rank exceeds the initial bound by R cannot be born before the rank-budget lower bound supplied by Theorem 15.
proof: Along each inference layer the rank increases by at most the declared increment, so reaching rank R requires enough layers to accumulate that increase.
intended_use: Provides a reusable way to prove search-depth lower bounds without enumerating all proofs.

title: Conservative macro compilation preserves the theorem set
statement: Under the hypotheses of conservative compilation, adjoining finitely many derived macro rules changes proof access but not ConF (Γ).
proof: Theorem 7.12 proves the compiled system conservative: each macro application expands to an original derivation, while original proofs remain legal.
intended_use: Makes a precise distinction between deductive strength and route shortening.

title: Every bounded-length proof appears in a bounded closure layer
statement: If φ has a proof from Γ of length at most m, then it is present by the finite proof layer guaranteed by Proposition 13.
proof: Proposition 13 relates proof length to the finite iterative closure construction.
intended_use: Connects syntactic certificate length with a closure-stage upper bound.

title: Right censoring yields a lower bound, not an exact unguided cost
statement: From EML (prcom) = 2633 and Eunguided (prcom) > 5000, one may conclude only Eunguided /EML > 5000/2633 ≈ 1.90, not the exact ratio.
proof: The unguided run stopped at the budget while still unknown, so its first-proof expansion count is known only to exceed the cutoff.
intended_use: Preserves the experiment’s finite, right-censored interpretation.

title: Unbounded finite width and failure of well-quasi-ordering
statement: For every m ≥ 1 there are m pairwise incomparable finitely describable degrees. The degree order on finitely describable machines is not a well-quasi-order.
proof: Take m distinct elements of the source infinite antichain. An enumeration of that antichain is an infinite sequence with no pair i < j satisfying ai ≤ aj, violating the defining sequence condition for a well-quasi-order.
intended_use: Identifies the specific order-theoretic obstruction supplied by the antichain.

title: Admissible self-awareness comparison is a preorder
statement: The admissible comparison is reflexive and transitive.
proof: Proposition 16.9 supplies identity and closure under composition of admissible translations; Proposition 16.10 lifts those facts to reflexivity and transitivity of the comparison relation.
intended_use: Provides the order-theoretic foundation for quotient degrees.

title: Permuting a finite breadth-first layer preserves first successful depth
statement: Suppose two searches expose exactly the same finite candidate histories in each depth layer, finish every shallower layer before the next, and differ only by permutations within each layer. If the least successful depth is d, both searches first succeed at depth d.
proof: No candidate in a depth below d succeeds, so either search must reach layer d. Each completely processes that finite layer unless it succeeds earlier within the layer; because it contains a successful candidate, both succeed there.
intended_use: Separates represented proof depth from within-layer discovery offset.

title: Undecidable consequence problems exclude computable finite-effective SICs
statement: If the consequence problem on an effectively presented domain is undecidable, then no computable deductively finitely effective SIC can solve it in the sense of the source framework.
proof: This is the contrapositive form recorded in Corollary 9.14: a computable finite-effective SIC would decide consequence by waiting for its finite completion stage.
intended_use: Marks the computability boundary of finite closure search.

title: The append-only derivation-state graph is acyclic
statement: For a fixed finite initial sequence of length m, every path of n transitions ends at a sequence of length m + n. Consequently the lifted graph has no directed cycles, and any reachable exact sequence state has a uniquely determined path length from the root.
proof: Each lifted transition appends one formula. Induction gives the length formula. A nonempty directed cycle would strictly increase sequence length and return to the same sequence, which is impossible.
intended_use: Supplies a genuine DAG for One-Step DAG mining.

title: The omega union of finite closure stages equals the consequence closure
statement: Under the stated inference-closed-domain hypotheses, the union of all finite exhaustive stages is exactly ConF (Γ).
proof: Every stage is sound, while Proposition 13 ensures each finite proof appears at some finite stage; Corollary 14 records equality.
intended_use: Explains why no separate transfinite stage is needed for ordinary finitary proof closure.

title: Conservative cooperation preserves dependence and independence status
statement: Under the same hypotheses, DepF,Bk (T) and IndF,Bk (T) are stage invariant.
proof: Both are defined from the two derivability predicates whose truth values are constant by Corollary 2.3.
intended_use: Shows that conservative BANK growth cannot settle an actually different object-theory question by changing premises.

title: The corrected target-search machine freezes without changing first hit
statement: For a provable target φ, freezing the target-search breadth-first SIC at its first hit preserves the first halting stage ∥φ∥F (Γ).
proof: C37 changes only post-halt state evolution: before the target is reached, the corrected state agrees with ordinary breadth-first search, and at the first hit it freezes.
intended_use: Isolates a SIC-axiom repair from the proof-horizon quantity itself.

title: Any accepted transition invariant holds at every global stage
statement: If a predicate Q holds at X0 and every accepted AMLD transition preserves Q, then Q(Xk) holds for all k ∈ N.
proof: This is Theorem 2.1 by ordinary induction on the global accepted-stage index.
intended_use: Provides the global analogue of single-ATP stage induction.

title: Proof paths give an upper bound on theorem-graph distance
statement: If a proof of φ from Γ induces a theorem-graph path of length n, then the directed graph distance from the start state to a φ-state is at most n.
proof: Proposition 6.8 turns the proof into a legal path. A shortest path cannot be longer than a displayed path.
intended_use: Connects certificates to graph-geometric upper bounds.

title: Resource replication restores wall-clock no-regret for a successful baseline
statement: If P receives the same processor, memory, verifier availability, and local service rate as the successful stand-alone prover, and foreign deposits may be ignored, then AMLD first-settlement wall time is at most the stand-alone proof time.
proof: Proposition 6.5 lets P reproduce the stand-alone run without resource loss; another role can only finish earlier.
intended_use: States exactly what extra resource assumption turns logical emulation into wall-clock dominance.

title: Exact reflection layers make the reflection index recoverable from birth stage
statement: For the reflection-closure machine of Theorem 20, the designated reflection formula θk is born at the exact layer stated by the theorem; hence different finite k have different recorded birth layers.
proof: Theorem 20 gives an exact formula for the layer as a strictly increasing function of k.
intended_use: Provides a calibrated benchmark in which semantic reflection depth and operational stage are linked exactly.

title: Policy replacement can change discovery cost while leaving theoremhood invariant
statement: Two ranking policies may inspect legal candidates in different orders and therefore use different numbers of expansions before finding a proof, while accepting exactly the same class of verifier-valid certificates.
proof: The proposition fixes theoremhood at the verifier boundary but leaves search order free. A permutation of a finite candidate set can move the first successful candidate to a different position.
intended_use: Separates search effort from deductive strength.

title: Local invariants extend to every finite accepted history
statement: If a predicate I holds at every allowed initial state and every accepted transition preserves I, then I holds at every finitely reachable accepted state, independently of the order in which enabled transitions are selected.
proof: Induct on history length. The zero-step case is the initial-state condition. For the inductive step, apply preservation to the final transition after the induction hypothesis at its predecessor.
intended_use: Provides the reusable proof form for typed BANK and verifier invariants.

title: Correct arithmetization transfers satisfying assignments to algebraic zeros
statement: Under the source arithmetization, a Boolean assignment satisfies the encoded propositional instance exactly when its 0–1 vector satisfies the associated polynomial constraints.
proof: This is the correctness equivalence of Proposition 10.35, read in both directions.
intended_use: Provides the verifier-safe bridge between propositional satisfiability and algebraic proof systems.

title: Each finite target horizon eventually stabilizes
statement: Under the BANK hypotheses above, if HFinf (B0, T) = h < ∞, then hk = HFinf (Bk, T) eventually becomes constant and has at most h strict decreases.
proof: The source theorem makes (hk) a nonincreasing sequence of nonnegative integers starting at h. Every strict decrease lowers it by at least one. There can be at most h such decreases, after the last of which the sequence is constant.
intended_use: Gives a targetwise convergence fact.

title: The admissible quotient contains an infinite strict chain
statement: There are quotient classes [M0 ] < [M1 ] < · · · under the source admissible self-awareness order.
proof: Corollary 16.20 supplies such a sequence using increasing reflection levels.
intended_use: Shows the quotient order has genuinely nontrivial infinite height.

title: Mutual admissible comparison is an equivalence relation
statement: The relation defined by comparison in both admissible directions is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.
proof: This is Proposition 16.12 applied to the underlying preorder.
intended_use: Licenses quotienting by presentation-level equivalence.

title: Not every set-theoretic SIC is computationally realizable
statement: Over an effectively coded domain there exist SICs that are not computable in the source sense.
proof: Corollary B.20 supplies the separation from the computable/Turing-realizable subclass.
intended_use: Preserves the distinction between the abstract SIC universe and executable machines.

title: Configuration provability is reachability
statement: In the configuration formal system, Γ ⊢FT c exactly when the source reachability condition for configuration c holds from Γ.
proof: Proposition B.5 proves the two directions between formal derivation and machine-transition reachability.
intended_use: Supplies a concrete bridge between proof systems and computation graphs.

title: Geodesic steps decrease remaining horizon exactly by one
statement: If 0 < h(S) < ∞, at least one successor U has h(U) = h(S) − 1. Every successor satisfies h(U) ≥ h(S) − 1.
proof: The finite minimum in LF-11.1 is attained because attainable finite distances are natural numbers. Its value is h(S) − 1, and all other values are at least that minimum.
intended_use: Gives an exact certificate target for a proposed geodesic next move.

title: A cardinality obstruction blocks synchronous equivalence in either direction
statement: If neither P(YM) injects into P(YN) nor P(YN) injects into P(YM), then M and N cannot be synchronously equivalent.
proof: Synchronous equivalence would contain a synchronous simulation in both directions. Proposition 3.11 would then supply both injections, contrary to hypothesis.
intended_use: Turns state-space cardinality into a quick negative certificate.

title: Finite inference-closed domains make exhaustive rule enumeration finitely complete
statement: If Y is finite and inference-closed, the canonical rule enumerator reaches its full consequence set after finitely many stages on every input.
proof: This is deductive finite effectiveness from Theorem 9.7. Monotone growth inside a finite powerset cannot add new formulas forever.
intended_use: Identifies a regime where exhaustive closure is guaranteed to stabilize.

title: A shortest-path ATP cannot beat intrinsic graph distance
statement: Under the finite/local hypotheses of the shortest-path ATP principle, no graph-search execution can first reach the target in fewer edge steps than the shortest-path distance.
proof: Theorem 6.9 identifies the optimal edge-step target cost with shortest-path search. Any successful execution is itself a path and hence has length at least the minimum.
intended_use: Provides a clean lower bound that is independent of heuristic ordering.

title: Conservative BANK growth can improve access without increasing deductive strength
statement: Along conservative BANK growth, the consequence closure remains ConF (B0) while the explicit-premise horizons for T, T −, and ⊥ are nonincreasing.
proof: Theorem 2.2 gives constant consequence closure; Theorem 5.1 gives nonincreasing shortest explicit-premise horizons under BANK inclusion.
intended_use: Summarizes the central ‘road-building without new axioms’ phenomenon of the corrected AMLD integration.

title: Tag-preserving simulation cannot decrease formal level
statement: Under the tag-preserving simulation hypotheses of Proposition 16.22, lev(M) ≤ lev(N).
proof: Proposition 16.22 preserves self-awareness statements; Corollary 16.23 records the resulting level inequality.
intended_use: Connects operational simulation to the syntactic level hierarchy under an explicit tag bridge.

title: Robust budget regions expand under safe enrichment
statement: Under that theorem’s preserved-state, controller-option, environment-response, target, and cost hypothe′ ses, every old state satisfying Hforce ≤ n also satisfies the post-enlargement bound Hforce ≤ n. ′
proof: The source theorem gives Hforce (s) ≤ Hforce (s) at every formerly forced-settling state. Apply this pointwise to the region bounded by n.
intended_use: Turns a pointwise monotonicity theorem into a budget-region inclusion.

title: Feasible interpolation turns suitable communication hardness into proof lower bounds
statement: Whenever the hypotheses of the source interpolation lower-bound theorem are met, hardness of the associated interpolant problem rules out small proofs in the proof system under consideration.
proof: This is the implication encoded by Theorem 10.28: a small proof plus feasible interpolation would yield an efficiently computable interpolant, contradicting the specified hardness premise.
intended_use: Shows how a semantic/combinatorial obstruction can become a proof-complexity lower bound.

title: Synchronous equivalence implies clocked equivalence
statement: If M ∼syn N, then M ∼ N under clocked deterministic simulation.
proof: Each synchronous simulation direction is, by Proposition 3.17, a clocked simulation direction. Mutuality is therefore preserved.
intended_use: Records the strict hierarchy between two simulation notions.

title: Order reflection suffices to transfer an antichain
statement: Let (Mi)i∈N be the source SIC antichain, and let J assign each Mi a GBG presentation. Suppose J(Mi) ⪯∗ J(Mj) =⇒ Mi ⪯clk Mj. Then the presentations J(Mi) are pairwise incomparable under ⪯∗.
proof: Any comparison between two distinct images would reflect to a forbidden comparison in the SIC antichain. The same argument excludes the reversed comparison.

title: High-rank deposits require enough cumulative certificate depth
statement: If a formula first deposited by update n has r(λ) > r0, then Qn ≥ ⌈(r(λ) − r0)/d⌉.
proof: Rearrange the upper bound r(λ) ≤ r0 + dQn from Theorem 8.1 and use integrality.
intended_use: Supplies a verifier-checkable lower bound on cooperative dependency work.

title: Admissible translations preserve each finite reflection stage
statement: Under an admissible translation, the image of the source reflection sequence is the corresponding reflection sequence in the target in the sense stated by Lemma 16.17.
proof: The lemma proves preservation inductively across the reflection construction.
intended_use: Provides the bridge needed to compare reflection levels across different syntactic presentations.

title: Object-level invariants are channel independent once the certificate is verified
statement: Whether a valid deposited lemma preserves an object invariant depends on its accepted certificate, not on whether P, R, D, I, or C happened to discover it.
proof: Corollary 3.3 is exactly this channel-independence consequence of certificate-preserved birth-time induction.
intended_use: Allows useful lemmas from a losing search role to be safely reused elsewhere.

title: Picard’s self-theory contains every finite reflection formula

proof: Theorem 20.4 gives level ω, hence provability of every finite θk under the source definition. Corollary 15.13 places each proved reflection formula in the self-theory.

title: Changing representatives does not change comparison
statement: If M ∼clk M ′ and N ∼clk N ′, then M ⪯clk N if and only if M ′ ⪯clk N ′.
proof: For the forward implication compose M ′ ⪯clk M ⪯clk N ⪯clk N ′. The reverse implication uses M ⪯clk M ′ ⪯clk N ′ ⪯clk N. Each chain uses transitivity of the source preorder.
intended_use: Makes a catalogue of degree comparisons independent of the chosen machine representative.

title: Two-stage deterministic hitting-time bound
statement: Under the two clocked embeddings of LF-28.1, assume target preservation at both embeddings. If the source hitting stage is n < ∞, the final target is hit by stage τ2 (τ1 (n)).
proof: Compose the state maps and target inclusions. The composite clock is bounded by LF-28.1. Apply the source hitting-time theorem to that composite witness.

title: Every advertised finite level and omega is realized
statement: For each n ∈ N and for ω as listed by the source, there exists a tagged ATP whose level is exactly that value.
proof: Theorem 15.32 supplies strict finite witnesses, and Corollary 15.33 records surjectivity of the level function onto the stated range.
